title: Doorway login routes elohim stewards through a peer-native OAuth portal; visible agency reflects their stewardship

vision_quotes.text: Doorway's relationship to identity is analogous to an OAuth relying party that presents the login portal but does not own it. Websites (doorways) present OAuth logins; identity providers (peer-native infrastructure) own them. ... Pre-graduation (hosted): the doorway serves as both relying party AND identity provider, because there is no peer-native identity yet. Post-graduation (peer-steward): the doorway is only the relying party. The login portal it presents is backed by the peer-native identity provider. Doorway never owns the peer-steward's login portal — it can only present it.

the p2p-native OAuth portal is rendered either (a) directly from the human's own steward device running elohim-app, or (b) by their trusted peer network rendering it on their behalf (mesh-rendered IdP — meaningful for recovery/availability when the steward device is unavailable).

M5 connects them via the account management surface in elohim-app (Surface 3 from project_imagodei_three_surfaces). ... Treat the hosted ↔ peer-native handoff as a first-class concern, not a side note. Do not foreclose the OAuth-pattern shape.

plan_deliverables.text: The doorway login form input accepts only the username portion (decorative @<gateway> suffix is enforced, not just a label). The user cannot type their full domain into the identifier field.
plan_deliverables.source: user-stated-bug 2026-05-22; current threshold-login.component.ts:86-101 renders the suffix but accepts full email and hints 'Or use your full email address'

plan_deliverables.text: When a returning user logs in to doorway and the auth response identifies them as a steward with a reachable portalHostUrl, doorway hands the session off to that portal host (the peer-native OAuth portal rendered from a trusted peer running elohim-app/elohim-storage) rather than completing the session locally.
plan_deliverables.source: project_m5_reframe_auth_portal_convergence.md + 2026-05-19-doorway-stewardship-chain-design.md §3.2-§3.3 (chain orphan + supersession); AuthResponse currently lacks portal_host_url field — ExchangeSessionResponse already has it (auth_routes.rs:88-103)

plan_deliverables.text: After login, the visible context label distinguishes 'hosted steward' (a steward currently accessing through a hosted doorway because their peer-native infra is unreachable or absent) from 'hosted visitor' (an unsgraduated hosted human). The visible label MUST not call a confirmed steward a visitor.
plan_deliverables.source: user-stated-bug 2026-05-22; current doorway-account.component.ts:97-106 renders a 'Accessing through {doorwayName}' banner only when isSteward && !hasLocalConductor — does not visibly assert role 'steward' anywhere; agency vocab in auth_routes.rs:142 lists 'doorway, node, device, hosted, visitor' but no 'steward' phase

plan_deliverables.text: Agency progression observed in the running UI is coherent with the canonical lifecycle expressed in the a2o features (auth-lifecycle, user-management, session-handoff, recovery-m5-doorway-handoff-to-steward) and with the M5 reframe: hosted → key_export → install_app → steward, with hosted-steward as the in-between state for a graduated steward visiting through doorway.

manifesto_anchors.why: If a graduated steward authenticates at doorway and doorway holds the identity authority (instead of yielding to the peer-native portal), the protocol's no-sovereignty / graduation principle is violated at the most visible surface. The user's identity authority is supposed to graduate away from doorway permanently. This is the M5 promise made visible.

Calling a confirmed steward a 'visitor' inverts the protocol's stance on agency. The label is the first signal a user has about whether the system understands who they are. Drift here means the substrate believes one thing and the UI tells the human a different thing — exactly the gap /deliver exists to close.

The doorway is offering hosting on its own gateway (alpha.elohim.host). Allowing arbitrary full domains in the identifier field invites users to mis-target, and confuses the federation surface (which is a separate 'Login with a different doorway' link). The form should express the doorway's scope, not pretend to be a generic identity provider.

scenarios_missing.intent: Threshold login identifier field rejects an identifier that already contains '@' (or strips the suffix); user can only type a username when the doorway provides the suffix.

When Matthew (steward with reachable portalHostUrl) logs in via threshold-login, doorway redirects him to the portal host for authentication (the peer-native OAuth portal renders the actual login decision), then resumes the doorway-side OAuth code dance back at the original client_id.

Visible context label after login distinguishes 'hosted steward' from 'hosted visitor' — Susan (hosted visitor) sees 'visitor' framing; Matthew (steward accessing via doorway because his node is offline) sees 'hosted steward' framing.

Agency progression panel in doorway-account is internally consistent with the auth lifecycle and M5 reframe — coverage scenarios for the four pipeline steps (hosted, key_export, install_app, steward) and the in-between 'hosted-steward' state when isSteward=true and hasLocalConductor=false.

screenshot_targets.what_should_be_visible: Identifier input is scoped to username only — typing '@something' is rejected or stripped. The decorative suffix '@alpha.elohim.host' is visible AND enforced (not just a hint). The 'Or use your full email address' hint is gone or reframed to point at the federated 'Login with a different doorway' link.

screenshot_targets.scenario: Steward login hands off to portal host
screenshot_targets.what_should_be_visible: After submitting credentials, the browser navigates to Matthew's reachable portalHostUrl (e.g. https://matthew.steward.example/...). Network panel shows a redirect with a session_token-like parameter. Doorway's OAuth code dance resumes at the registered client_id after the portal-host completes the decision.

Visible 'Hosted Steward' (or similar) badge/label near the account header. The 'Accessing through {doorwayName}' banner is present. The agency pipeline shows step 4 'Steward' as not-yet-completed (since the user is on hosted infrastructure) but step 1 'Hosted' as completed AND the role is correctly named.
Visible 'Hosted Visitor' or 'Visitor' framing. Agency pipeline shows step 1 'Hosted' as the current state. Graduation CTA visible.
